status_summary: Defense Department accession standards exclude HIV-positive applicants, and a 2024 district court injunction in Wilkins v. Hegseth barred applying that bar to asymptomatic applicants with undetectable viral loads. A Fourth Circuit panel stayed the injunction on 2025-12-09, the department paused initial training for HIV-positive recruits in January 2026, and the panel reversed the injunction in February 2026; the full court granted rehearing en banc on 2026-05-18, vacating the panel decision and lifting the stay, and on 2026-06-25 voted 11 to 4 to grant the government a partial stay limited to the injunction's reach beyond the three individual plaintiffs. A Coast Guard bulletin of 2026-07-13 cites a Department of War exception-to-policy memo of 2026-06-17 that admits applicants with suppressed HIV to comply with the court order, and the bulletin was issued after the partial stay. No change to the Defense Department medical standards instruction or NDAA provision on HIV was found.

timeline.event: A Fourth Circuit panel heard argument in Wilkins v. Hegseth and the same day stayed enforcement of the 2024 injunction on its own initiative (as recited in the en banc order of 2026-06-25).
timeline.source: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit

timeline.event: The Office of the Secretary of Defense directed a pause on initial training for newly enlisted HIV-positive recruits while accession policy was reviewed, per Military Entrance Processing Command guidance (article dated 2026-01-17; the directive was sent on the preceding Friday, 2026-01-16, an inferred date).
A three-judge Fourth Circuit panel reversed the 2024 injunction in Wilkins v. Hegseth, holding the military may rely on medical standards that disqualify people with HIV.
The Fourth Circuit granted rehearing en banc in Wilkins v. Hegseth, vacating the panel decision (date as recited in the en banc order of 2026-06-25).
timeline.source: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit

timeline.event: The Fourth Circuit's lifting of the panel stay took effect following the en banc grant, so the injunction again applied in full.

The Under Secretary for Personnel and Readiness issued an exception-to-policy memo admitting asymptomatic applicants with suppressed HIV to comply with the Wilkins court order (as cited in a Coast Guard bulletin).

The en banc Fourth Circuit, 11 to 4, granted the government's motion for a partial stay pending appeal, which sought to stay the injunction to the extent it applies beyond the three individual plaintiffs.
timeline.source: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit
